back: Mean: sum ÷ number. Median: middle ordered value. Mode: most frequent value or category.
Upper quartile − lower quartile: the spread of the middle 50%, unaffected by extremes.
(new − old) ÷ old × 100; positive = increase, negative = decrease.
Rate = events ÷ population × 1 000, e.g. 945 births in 35 000 people = 27 per 1 000.
Ratio compares parts (3 : 2); proportion compares a part with the whole (0.4 or 40%).
Count s.f. from the first non-zero digit (38 451 → 38 000 at 2 s.f.); 4 600 000 = 4.6 × 10⁶.
Interpolation: estimate within the data (safer). Extrapolation: estimate beyond it (riskier).
Small or non-random samples, untypical timing, instrument precision, old secondary data, misleading presentation.
